text:
anna: noticed spike in mTLS handshake errors across eu-west and us-east at ~14:22 UTC. lots of keystore decrypt denials in rotator logs.
paul: logs?
sara: paste (redacted):
```
2026-07-08T14:22:34Z rotator-eu-2 ERROR cert: unseal failed: KMS.Decrypt AccessDenied for key arn:aws:kms:eu-west-1:123:key/rot-2026
  at keystore.Seal/Unseal (rotator.go:148)
  at proxy/handshake (handshake.go:76)
```
lee: CloudTrail shows kms:Decrypt denied for principal arn:aws:iam::123:role/rotator-service-prod. But we rotated the CMK yesterday and tightened key policy to explicit ARNs.
anna: we also pushed a CI change that swapped the pod IAM role annotation to a new role alias `rotator-prod-v2` at 14:18. Might not match key policy.
paul: so key policy expects rotator-service-prod but instances are requesting as rotator-prod-v2 -> AccessDenied. That explains it.
sara: mitigation steps: A) relax CMK policy to include both role ARNs (fast), B) revert pod role alias (requires deploy), C) bootstrap a cross-account decrypt relay (slow). Which quickest?
lee: A is fastest but touches key policy and compliance. Need SOC rubber stamp. B is safer but slower.
anna: I'll open a temporary CMK allowlist change and page SOC. Tag logs with incident id inc-1769999991.
infra-bot: change request: temp-keypolicy-allow rotator-prod-v2 -> https://git.internal/infra/kms/pull/501 (waiting approval).
oncall: SOC/approvers?
soc-bot: SOC notified; require justification and timeline for policy relaxation. Provide CloudTrail slice and timeline.
paul: if we relax policy, limit to a 1-hour TTL and log all decrypt calls. We can revert after deploy.
sara: approved by infra-ops at 14:26, temp allow applied 14:27:05. Rotator decrypts succeeded ~14:27:30; handshake errors dropped 88% by 14:30.
anna: mitigation done. Now root cause: deployment switched pod role alias without syncing KMS key policies. We need a stronger deploy guard.
lee: follow-ups: 1) add CI preflight that fetches CMK policy and verifies new pod role ARN is allowed before rollout, 2) implement a KMS principal allowlist manifest in infra repo and require two approvers for changes, 3) add a rolling test harness that simulates cert unseal in each region using the exact IAM role the pod will assume, 4) enrich tracing so `trace_id` in handshake logs maps to CloudTrail event ids.
paul: recommend also adding a short-lived proxy-side cache and staged certificate refresh backoff so a brief KMS deny doesn't take down all nodes. e.g., keep existing cert valid for +5m and jittered refresh.
sara: agree. We'll add a metric: percent of proxies reporting `keystore.unseal:AccessDenied` over 3m; if >5% page infra and auto-open a temp keypolicy change with required approvers. Detection example: `sum(rate(kms_decrypt_denied_total{region=~"eu-.*|us-.*"}[3m])) / sum(up{job="proxy",region=~"eu-.*|us-.*"}) > 0.05`
lee: compliance / SOC: we have audit logs showing denies only. No successful decrypts by unauthorized principals. SOC requested full CloudTrail export for 14:00-15:00 UTC and a short RCA note.
oncall: incident filed INC-2026-07001 assigned to @anna (deploy guard) and @paul (proxy backoff).
anna: will draft PR for CI preflight and the cross-check script.
paul: one more: should proxy treat KMS AccessDenied as 5xx or 403? If 5xx, clients retry and timeouts hide auth problems; 403 surfaces quickly. Keep 403 but add a specific `x-keystore-diagnostic` header so ops can trigger the correct rollback runbook.
sara: noted. Closing thread, monitor for residual errors. Reopen if new denials show up. :white_check_mark:
